messages.subject: glgm (generalized linear geostatistical model) in inla?
messages.subject_clean: glgm (generalized linear geostatistical model) in inla?
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am modelling presence/absence data as a function of trend + spatial component using logit link function according to glgm specification described as:

g(E [Y(x)|S(·)]) = S(x) = d(x)^T*beta + U(x)

where S(.) is a signal process at spatial location x which is a spatially dependent random variable.
Spatial dependency in S(.) is passed on through component U(.) which is a spatially dependent, normally distributed random variable, which has an expected value of zero everywhere, a variance equal to sigma^2 and correlation function rho(h).

d(x)^T*beta is a spatial trend that stores the values of explanatory variables at spatial location and a vector of model coefficients that indicate the relationship between the covariates and S(.). This means that expected value of  S(.) is not constant in space, but varies as a function of the covariates.

I want to compare the results of this model with inla and I am wondering if there already exists an implementation of this type of model or someone could point it out any tips?

Many thanks,
OIga

messages.body_plain:
On 03/06/13 15:58, Olga Lyashevska wrote:
> I am modelling presence/absence data as a function of trend + spatial
> component using logit link function according to glgm specification
> described as:
>
> g(E [Y(x)|S(�)]) = S(x) = d(x)^T*beta + U(x)

Yes, that is a standard situation.  There may be examples for precisely
this kind of model already on r-inla.org <http://r-inla.org>.  The Cameletti et al
case-study available there has similar bout more complex structure; it
has a space-time model and Gaussian instead of Binomial data, but the
essential inla approach would be very similar for your model.
Also see the tutorial texts about using SPDE models.

The basic structure in inla to get this mode will look something like
this (a lot more details in the tutorials...):

spde = ...
formula = y ~ covariates + f(spatial, model=spde)
... = inla(..., family="binomial")

Finn

messages.subject: factor analysis model using INLA
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am wondering if we can fit a factor analysis model with INLA?
A factor analysis model can be also seen as a generalized linear mixed model with a Gaussian latent variable which is multiplied by a factor loading.
For example, the model looks like
(for binary response)
logit (y_ij=1 | th_j) =  a_i*th_j + b_i * x_i ,   th_j ~ N(0, var)

y_ij: response to item i for person j
a_i : factor loading for item (indicator) i
th_j : latent variable for person j
b_i: regression coefficient for a covariate x_i

If we can fit such a model above, how can we set up INLA for this.
Any of your comments/suggestions would be appreciated.   Thank you very much!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Precision parameters are very high. Is there an explanation?
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] Precision parameters are very high. Is there an explanation?
messages.body_plain:
The key, pointed on the link (#20) at http://www.r-inla.org/faq, is that
we have a strong prior sensitivity. So it need carefull on the prior
choise. For example, considering the reproducible example on that link,
see the results bellow using two different priors

res1 <- inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model="iid",
hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(1,1)))),
       data =data.frame(y,idx), family = "binomial", Ntrials = 1)
res1$summary.hy

res2 <- inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model="iid",
hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(0.1,0.1)))),
       data =data.frame(y,idx), family = "binomial", Ntrials = 1)
res2$summary.hy

we have different results...
